text.p: Russia expressed satisfaction on Monday with Bosnia's first post-war elections, saying they laid the foundation for peace and economic reconstruction.

"A very important step has been taken in the process of normalising the lives of all the peoples of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the preconditions have been created for further advancing the peace process and for economic and social renewal," the foreign ministry said in a statement.
It praised the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) for its organisation of the ballot, noting turnout had been around 70 percent and polling had gone fairly smoothly.
"Ahead lie no less difficult tasks: the formation and start of work by local authorities," the statement said, adding Russia would continue to work to help to fulfill the Dayton peace deal.
Preliminary results from balloting for a three-person Bosnian presidency from Moslem, Serb and Croat communities as well as inter-ethnic parliaments are due later on Monday.
